Rachel / team —

Quick technical checklist and repro notes (attachment: repro-checklist.md). High level:

1) Model variant: we'll serve the customer model in fp16 as the default; int8 quantized variant is available but there is a known 6-8% quality delta for a small subset of prompts (we should include the example prompt set to validate). We'll publish both endpoints and annotate the MAP with quality tradeoffs.

2) Tooling differences:
  - Wrk vs Locust: wrk produces lower-overhead open-loop throughput numbers; Locust (our preferred open-source load generator) runs closed-loop tasks and will reflect TTL/think-time accurately. For parity, we'll provide a small Locust script that mirrors the wrk scenario (see repro-checklist.md).
  - Measurement alignment: ensure both sides emit a trace header X-RW-TRACE-ID. We'll collect per-request durations and GPU metrics (utilization, mem bw) at 1s granularity.

3) Cold-start / TTFT: TTFT should be measured as time from request to first token on the stream (not full completion) and captured separately for cold and warm paths (cold = empty KV cache + new container). We'll run a 10-minute warmup for steady-state metrics and run explicit cold-start probes (5 runs) interleaved.

4) Concurrency approach: for the 200 interactive users profile we'll advise a ramp of 1s/user up to 200 users, track p50/p95 and error rate at each 25-user bin.

5) Competitive baseline: Aperture AI (publicly reported) showed p95 ~ 420ms at 100 rps on a T4-like configuration — direct comparisons need careful normalization (model size, seq length). We'll include a normalization appendix in the MAP.

Action items: Ben creates Locust task (including X-RW-TRACE-ID header) by 6/25; Marissa will prepare results template; I'll verify int8 profile and attach the quantization notes.

-Karthik

Subject: MAP update: co-run results & reconciliation (Nova Health)

Team / Jordan —

We completed the co-run on 6/29. Summary (high level) and next steps — full artifacts attached (map-results-summary.xlsx):

Results summary (representative):
- Profile A (50 rps sustained, batching allowed):
  - Throughput: 48.3 rps observed
  - p50 latency: 86 ms; p95 latency: 198 ms
  - TTFT (warm): p50 12 ms; p95 34 ms
  - Error rate: 0.2% (transient connection resets during aggressive batching)
- Profile B (200 concurrent interactive users):
  - Observed effective concurrency: 196 users (ramp target hit)
  - p50 latency: 94 ms; p95 latency: 412 ms
  - TTFT (cold probes): mean 420 ms (cold), warm p95 118 ms

Methodology divergences identified:
1) Load generator behavior: Nova's Locust closed-loop ramp produced slightly higher p95 vs our open-loop wrk baseline. We aligned by running the same Locust script (Ben) in both environments; after alignment numbers moved ~5-8% closer.
2) Quantization: int8 variant reduced memory pressure but introduced a 7% degrade on prompt set #3; we recommend shipping fp16 for the POC and offering int8 as an optimization with explicit QA gating.
3) Cold-start measurement mismatch: Nova's initial probe measured full-response time; we clarified TTFT definition (first token on stream) and re-labeled the MAP metrics accordingly.

Competitive note: after normalization for sequence length and model variant, we see Aperture AI public baseline comparable at p95 but higher cost per token in their published configuration — full competitive appendix attached.

Next steps / MAP updates:
- Marissa to upload map-results-summary.xlsx and updated redwood_map_v2.pdf (includes reconciliation notes) by 7/1.
- Karthik to provide quantization appendix and int8 caveat language.
- Rachel to confirm Q3 decision threshold language with Jordan and procurement.

Jordan — thanks for the collaborative run. If you want a step-by-step repro for the int8 discrepancy we can schedule a focused debug session next week.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
